prompt: Design an accessibility system for a controller-first action game across menus, HUD, tutorials, combat cues, communication, pause/settings, and error recovery. The game supports dialogue and non-speech audio cues, fast visual events, camera motion, remappable controls, online co-op, and a dense upgrade menu. Produce a platform-appropriate accessibility design and validation matrix rather than applying a browser checklist.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Required menu and gameplay actions remain reachable with remappable/controller-compatible input without introducing an input trap or requiring one fixed physical control where the platform permits alternatives.

Dialogue, non-speech audio cues, fast visual events, combat/status cues, and communication define redundant or configurable channels so critical gameplay information is not conveyed by sound, color, or brief motion alone.

Camera/motion intensity, text/readability, HUD information, timing-sensitive prompts, and dense upgrade-menu navigation have concrete configuration or equivalent-access requirements without removing the core gameplay objective.

Validation spans representative menu, tutorial, combat, co-op communication, pause/settings, and recovery tasks across named input/accessibility configurations and identifies which hardware/runtime combinations remain unverified.

The design uses game/platform accessibility guidance as requirements or best-practice evidence where applicable, does not import DOM/CSS/browser mechanics, and does not convert guidance into an unsupported compliance claim.

evidence: representative gameplay and menu task matrix
XAG-style guidance treated as best practice not compliance
